page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-240GB-1xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor with 12 vCPUs and 12 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU with 80 GB of VRAM. Notably, this instance does not include local storage, requiring external storage attachments.

Benchmark data highlights strong capabilities in specific workloads. The server achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 35.51 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.51 GB/sec, alongside strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 182.09 GB/sec. For artificial intelligence workloads, the NVIDIA H100 GPU delivers top-tier LLM inference speeds, processing 10515.12 tokens per second for prompts and generating 547.27 tokens per second using a small 135M model. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Passmark, fall within the average range, with a Passmark CPU score of 32078.76 and a database operations score of 12843.58.

The server hardware profile presents distinct tradeoffs. While the GPU and memory capacity are substantial, the CPU allocation is shared, which may introduce performance variability under sustained, non-GPU-bound CPU-intensive tasks. The lack of local storage requires architectural planning for data-intensive applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of memory relative to the 12 vCPUs, combined with a premium Hopper-class GPU, positions this server as a specialized resource for GPU-accelerated tasks rather than general-purpose compute. It is highly suited for deep learning, LLM inference, data science pipelines, and advanced matrix-based mathematical modeling utilizing Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets.

This server is best suited for machine learning inference, data science, and matrix-heavy mathematical computations where high VRAM and system memory are critical.
